{{Short description|Mathematical Quadratic formula}}
In mathematical finite group theory, a '''quadratic pair''' for the odd [[prime number|prime]] ''p'', introduced by {{harvtxt|Thompson|1971}}, is a finite [[group (mathematics)|group]] ''G'' together with a '''quadratic module''', a [[faithful representation]] ''M'' on a [[vector space]] over the [[finite field]] with ''p'' elements such that ''G'' is generated by elements with [[minimal polynomial (linear algebra)|minimal polynomial]] (''x''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1)<sup>2</sup>. Thompson classified the quadratic pairs for ''p''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;5. {{harvtxt|Chermak|2004}} classified the quadratic pairs for ''p''&nbsp;=&nbsp;3. With a few exceptions, especially for ''p''&nbsp;=&nbsp;3, groups with a quadratic pair for the prime ''p'' tend to be more or less [[groups of Lie type]] in characteristic&nbsp;''p''.
